chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Jamil, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: What is the condition regarding the animal? He said: Three days for the buyer. I asked: And what is the condition for that which is not an animal? He said: The two parties to the sale have the option (to cancel) as long as they have not separated. When they separate, there is no option after their mutual consent.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the return period for animals and other goods in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* delineates the specific duration of the 'option of the session' (*khiyar al-majlis*) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between livestock and other commodities. It establishes a three-day window for animals, reflecting practical considerations for their care and inspection, while general goods remain subject to cancellation until the parties physically separate, emphasizing mutual consent as the condition for finalizing the contract.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-128 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Jamil, on the authority of Fuzayl ibn Yasar that he asked Aba Abdullah Imam as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “What is the condition for dealing when buying an animal?”

The Imam (MGB) replied, “The buyer has three days (to return it if he doesn’t want it).” Then he asked, “And what are the conditions for buying things other than an animal?” The Imam (MGB) replied, “Either the buyer or the seller has the right to call off the deal before they separate. Once they separate, they cannot call off the deal unless both sides agree.”
